summary: Embedded dashboard alert context truncated for long time-range snapshots
description:
Issue summary:
Customers embedding Redwood dashboards into third-party portals see alert context (tracehook links and the contextual query snippet) truncated or missing when the dashboard snapshot uses a large time range (>90 days). The symptom is visible on both the embedded iframe and when exporting a scheduled snapshot PDF.

Impact:
- Fathom Health reports that scheduled alert notifications no longer contain the drilldown tracehook for high-severity alerts tied to nightly batch failures.
- Embedded dashboards show the alert card but the "Open in Redwood" link arrives with a truncated ?tracehook= token, resulting in 404/expired link when opened from email/slack.
- Affects enterprise customers who rely on long-range retrospectives and scheduled reports.

Environment:
- prod (us-east primary), also reproduced in eu-west for a separate org.
- Console release: v3.19.2 (web-frontend), alerting-service: v2.8.1, tracehook-proxy: v1.4.0.

Steps to reproduce:
1) In an enterprise org with many monthly rollups, create a dashboard with an alert rule that includes a tracehook (trace_id/link) and set the query time range to 6 months.
2) Embed the dashboard via the embed token (org-scoped) into an external app.
3) Trigger the alert (or run a scheduled snapshot) and inspect the alert payload in the notification (email / scheduled PDF / Slack webhook).
4) Click the drilldown link that should open the console with the tracehook parameter.

Observed result:
- The tracehook query parameter is truncated or ends mid-token. Console shows "Missing trace context" and the linked time window is incorrectly bounded. Exported PDF shows the alert card without the link.

Expected result:
- Full tracehook token preserved in embeds and scheduled exports regardless of the snapshot time range. Alert notification should provide a valid link back to console with context preserved.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create dashboard with alert containing a tracehook; 2) Set dashboard time range >= 90 days; 3) Embed dashboard; 4) Trigger alert or wait for scheduled snapshot; 5) Open notification link and observe tracehook parameter
logs:
Excerpt from tracehook-proxy logs (2026-03-12T07:58:11Z):
[WARN] request: /api/alert/payload id=abc123 size=4821 bytes - url-length=8123; token-trimmed=true
[ERROR] embed-signer: encode failed: truncation at 8192 bytes for org=org-987
Console front-end (v3.19.2) reported: RangeError: URI too long when constructing embed URL containing long snapshot query string
investigation_notes:
Support confirmed reproduction in a staging org. Initial hypothesis: embed signing and tokenization path uses a fixed URL buffer or backend field trimmed at 8KB during snapshot serialization. The scheduled exporter compresses the alert context but does not base64-encode long tracehook payloads, which leads to mid-token truncation when persisted to the snapshots table.
Checked DB: snapshots.metadata for Fathom Health shows 'alert_context' blob length 8192 and trailing '...' appended by serializer.
Relevant PR touching serializer: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4329 merged 2026-02-28 (optimize snapshot size) — may have introduced aggressive truncation logic.
Temporary reproduction note: reducing dashboard range to 30 days preserves full token; artificially expanding event aggregation (high-cardinality tags) increases token size causing truncation.

resolution: Workaround provided: reduce snapshot time-window to <90 days or disable tracehook in scheduled alerts. Engineering to land encoding+schema-change fix: base64-encode alert context and migrate snapshot.metadata column to MEDIUMBLOB. Patch branch created: fix/snapshot-context-encoding (PR #4521). Planned rollout: stage patch 2026-03-18, prod rollout 2026-03-21 after migration backfill. Post-deploy: run reconciliation job to re-encode existing truncated snapshot contexts.
next_steps: 1) Eng to get PR #4521 reviewed and merged. 2) DB migration plan: alter table snapshots.metadata to MEDIUMBLOB (SRE to run during low-traffic window). 3) Backfill/reconcile truncated entries using graceful re-encoding job. 4) Notify customers when fixed and confirm embedded alert links are valid. 5) Add test to prevent regressions: assert tracehook preserved for time ranges up to 12 months.
